lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 4 you met capital letters. Which words always start with a capital? The first word of a sentence, and names of people, places and days.
When you write the title of a work, you show that it is a title.
Long works, like books, films, plays and albums, go in italics when typed, or are underlined when written by hand.
Short works, like songs, poems, short stories and chapters, go in quotation marks: My favourite poem is "The Owl and the Pussy-cat".
Use capitals for the important words in a title: The Wind in the Willows. Small words like the, and, in and of stay lower case unless they come first.
Try it in the world: make a sign for your world's library: a book title in capitals where they belong, and a poem's title in quotation marks. Next: writing an opinion piece.

exercises.prompt: How do you show a song's title?
exercises.hint: A song is a short work.
exercises.explain: Short works go in quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: How do you show a book's title when typing?
exercises.hint: A book is a long work.
exercises.explain: Long works are typed in italics.

exercises.prompt: A poem's title goes in quotation marks.
exercises.hint: A poem is short.
exercises.explain: Yes: short works go in quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: How do you show a film's title when writing by hand?
exercises.hint: You can't write italics by hand.
exercises.explain: By hand, underline long works.

exercises.prompt: Which is a short work?
exercises.hint: Which is shortest?
exercises.explain: A song is a short work.

exercises.prompt: Which title is capitalised correctly?
exercises.hint: Important words get capitals.
exercises.explain: Wind and Willows get capitals; in and the stay small.

exercises.prompt: Which is written correctly?
exercises.hint: A song is a short work. Which marks go round a short work's title?
choices: We sang "Row Your Boat" in class.
We sang Row Your Boat in class.
We sang (Row Your Boat) in class.
exercises.explain: Song titles go in quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: A book has a chapter called Into the Cave. How do you show the chapter's title?
exercises.hint: A chapter is part of a book.
exercises.explain: Chapters are short works: quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: In a title, small words like "and" and "of" stay lower case unless they come first.
exercises.hint: Look at The Wind in the Willows: which words are small?
exercises.explain: Yes: small words stay lower case unless they come first.

exercises.prompt: Which is a long work, shown in italics?
exercises.hint: Which is longest?
exercises.explain: A play is a long work.

exercises.prompt: Which title is capitalised correctly?
exercises.hint: The first word always gets a capital.
choices: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth
A journey To The centre of the earth
a Journey to the Centre of the Earth
exercises.explain: A, Journey, Centre and Earth get capitals; to, the and of stay small.

exercises.prompt: A poem called The Tiger is in a book called Animal Poems. How is each title shown?
exercises.hint: Short work, long work.
choices: the poem in quotation marks; the book in italics
exercises.explain: The poem (short) in quotation marks; the book (long) in italics.

exercises.prompt: A song title should be in italics.
exercises.hint: Is a song long or short?
exercises.explain: No: songs go in quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: Why do we mark titles in writing?
exercises.hint: Think of a title in the middle of a sentence.
choices: so readers know it's the name of a work
exercises.explain: Marking titles shows they are names of works.

exercises.prompt: Which word should be lower case? "Stars Of Winter"
exercises.hint: A small word, not first.
exercises.explain: Of is a small word in the middle: Stars of Winter.

exercises.prompt: Sort the works: italics or quotation marks?
exercises.hint: Long works go in italics; short works in quotation marks.
exercises.explain: Books, films and plays are long works: italics. Songs, poems and chapters are short: quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: Build the title with its capitals right: put the words in order.
exercises.hint: The important words have capitals; the small words stay small in the middle.
exercises.explain: Stars in the Winter: Stars and Winter get capitals; in and the stay small.

exercises.prompt: Sort the works: italics or quotation marks when you type their titles?
exercises.hint: Is it a long, whole work, or a short piece that sits inside something bigger?
exercises.explain: Albums, magazines and TV series are long works: italics. A short story, a chapter and a poem are short: quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: Build a second title with its capitals right: put the words in order.
exercises.hint: Find the word whose capital can start the title; the small word stays in the middle.
exercises.explain: The Map of Treasure Island: The starts it with a capital, Map, Treasure and Island are important words, and of stays small in the middle.

exercises.prompt: How many words need a capital in the title "the lion and the mouse"?
exercises.hint: The first word always gets one; after that, only the important words.
exercises.explain: The Lion and the Mouse: The (the first word), Lion and Mouse. And and the second the stay small: 3 capitals.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: is the title shown correctly?
exercises.hint: Only short works go in quotation marks. Is each one long or short?
exercises.explain: Correct: a poem and a song are short works, so quotation marks. Not correct: a film and an album are long works, so they need italics (or underlining by hand), not quotation marks.

exercises.prompt: "Journey to the Centre of the Earth": sort the words.
exercises.hint: Small words like to, the and of stay lower case unless they come first.
exercises.explain: Journey, Centre and Earth are important words, so they get capitals. To, the and of are small words in the middle, so they stay lower case.
